_source: Rise Fall Repeat Short, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-19: frames at 0/0.5/1/1.5/2/2.5/3 s then every 3 s to the end (shot edges to about 1.5 s), word timings from YouTube's caption track. Our own descriptions. Every picture is a generated period still (sepia 1890s), slow push. Not probed for sound (owner: probe one only; same channel and mix as vBw4jNaJQ28).

hook.firstFrame: a period salesman in a bowler hat handing a small package to a man on a street, warm sepia; 2-3 word white caption
hook.firstLine: a man gave his product away and ended up with a giant company

shots.picture: period salesman handing a free package to a customer on a street
the salesman standing over a heap of gold coins with a globe, golden light
a young man with a suitcase on a rainy 1890s city street
the salesman at a doorway with a tray of soap bars
shop counters stacked with soap and baking-powder tins, customers
the salesman holding up gum packs beside tins at a counter
a crowded store, shoppers reaching for gum packs
shopkeepers in aprons asking for more gum
partners in suits arguing across a table
the man alone at a desk studying gum packs and ledgers
two flavour packs held up close over the desk
a crowd under a 'PANIC OF 1907' newspaper headline board
the man counting bank notes at his desk
a shop wall of branded gum displays, owner smiling
two men shaking hands in front of a buyer's and the brand's signs
the man at his desk with gum packs, warm lamp light

lines.gist: he handed his product out free and built a giant company by accident
a young salesman arrives in a big city almost broke, selling soap door to door
nobody wanted soap, so a free extra sold it, and he switched to the extra
he did it again with a small free sweet nobody thought was a business
buyers began asking only for the freebie; it outsold the real product
partners mocked it, but he dropped everything else and went all in
he launched two flavours and in a crash borrowed heavily for advertising
it became the country's top seller; the company is finally named
decades later a rival bought it for a huge sum
lesson: the best opportunity can hide in your smallest offer

ending.lastFrame: the founder at his desk with product packs and a 3-word caption

whyItWorks: The brand is withheld until the last 12 seconds, so the name itself is the reveal.
The end figure is teased in the first 3 seconds and repaid at the end (a closed loop of curiosity).
Each beat is one small, concrete step (soap, then baking powder, then gum) told in short punchy lines.
A new still every 3-6 s with a slow push and a hit on each cut keeps a 2-minute Short moving.
